title: Multidimensional SLO Metering and Billing Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the product approach and operational steps for billing customers based on a multidimensional SLO metering model. The goal is to enable commercialization of latency/fidelity/availability SLAs as first-class metered dimensions, provide deterministic quoteability for Dedicated/Private, and support progressive rollout through self-serve and pilot programs.

Intended audience
- Product managers (pricing, consumption)
- Finance and RevOps
- Backend billing & metering engineers
- Solutions & customer success teams running pilots

Goals
- Define a minimal viable SKU and telemetry schema to meter per-request SLO consumption.
- Provide migration guidance for existing token-based customers to opt into SLO-backed plans without revenue disruption.
- Establish a pilot and rollout sequence with guardrails to limit revenue leakage and customer impact.

Scope and non-goals
- Scope: hosted and dedicated offerings, per-request metering for text generation, chat sessions, and embeddings. Includes SLA dimensions: latency (p50/p95), fidelity (model-capability tier), and availability (successful completion rate).
- Non-goals: marketplace rev-share contract changes, third-party vendor cost allocation (handled separately).

Key terms and definitions
- SLO Dimension: a measurable property used for billing (latency, fidelity, availability).
- Fidelity Tier: discrete quality buckets (baseline, enhanced, gold) mapped to model variants and quantization profiles.
- Meter Unit: the atomic billing unit. For this playbook, one Meter Unit equals one request attributed to an SLO band (see SKU matrix).

Design overview
- Metering model: Each request is evaluated against configured SLO thresholds and assigned a single SKU label (combination of latency-band, fidelity-tier, availability status). Billing increments are by Meter Unit, with optional token add-on for very large responses.
- Attribution: Tenant-level and per-route attribution supported. Route overrides (per-route SLO budgets) are used to drive developer UX and quota enforcement.
- Fallback handling: If a request falls back to a lower fidelity variant due to capacity, the billing attribution preserves the requested fidelity for a configurable grace window (default: 30s).

Minimal SKU matrix (example)
| SKU ID | Latency band | Fidelity tier | Availability band | Price per meter unit (USD) | Notes |
|--------|--------------|---------------|------------------|---------------------------|-------|
| SLO-LB-BASE | p95 <= 250ms | baseline | success >= 99.9% | 0.0008 | Default, low-cost |
| SLO-LB-ENH | p95 <= 200ms | enhanced | success >= 99.95% | 0.0025 | Higher-perf model |
| SLO-LB-GOLD | p95 <= 120ms | gold | success >= 99.99% | 0.0060 | Premium commit only |
| SLO-LB-DEGRADED | p95 > 250ms | baseline | success >= 98% | 0.0005 | Grace/best-effort fallback |

Note: Pricing numbers are illustrative for pilot planning. Final rates require finance approval.

Telemetry and event contract
- Every request emits a single metering event with the following JSON payload (example):

```json
{
  "request_id": "uuid-1234",
  "tenant_id": "acct-789",
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "timestamp": "2026-09-15T14:22:30Z",
  "latency_ms": 132,
  "latency_band": "p95<=200ms",
  "fidelity_tier": "enhanced",
  "availability": "success",
  "meter_units": 1,
  "token_estimate": 42
}
```

- Implementation notes: latency_band is computed against the request's observed latency at completion. For streaming responses the p95 window is computed on request end-to-end.

Billing and reporting behavior
- Billing window: daily cumulative aggregation of meter events at tenant level, exported to billing pipeline with both raw events and aggregated rollups (per-tenant, per-route, per-day).
- Invoicing: invoices include a breakdown by SLO SKU, route-level top consumers, and any overage adjustments.
- Dispute flow: disputes trigger an auto-capture of raw events for the disputed period and a replayable audit log.

Migration strategy (high level)
1. Pilot phase (Q4 2026) — Closed pilot with 3–5 customers: test telemetry fidelity and invoice previews.
2. Opt-in self-serve (Q1 2027) — Allow customers to enable SLO metering in the Console for selected routes; show simulated cost estimates for 30/60/90 days.
3. Default for new Dedicated contracts (Q2 2027) — Offer SLO-backed SKUs as the default commercial option for new Dedicated purchases.
4. Migration window (Q3–Q4 2027) — Incentivized migration for token-based customers with a crediting program and a 6-month grace period.

Pilot runbook (operational checklist)
- Pre-pilot tasks
  - Confirm telemetry schema ingestion to billing test pipeline (owner: billing eng).
  - Define pilot success KPIs (see Metrics).
  - Prepare invoice-preview UI mockups and legal terms for trial.
- Onboarding steps
  1. Provision pilot tenant with feature-flag "slo_billing_v1".
  2. Enable debug-level metering events and sample retention for 90 days.
  3. Run 14-day synthetic traffic and compare simulated billing to historical token-billing baseline.
  4. Share invoice-preview with customer and collect feedback.
- Escalation
  - If unexpected >10% variance vs estimated billing for pilot customers, pause gate and invoke Product & Finance review.

Metrics and KPIs to track
- Accuracy: percentage of metering events successfully ingested (target >= 99.5%).
- Revenue delta: forecasted vs actual billing for pilot customers (target within ±5% after tuning).
- Customer impact: number of functional regressions tied to SLO enforcement during pilot (target 0).
- Adoption: % of eligible routes enabled for SLO metering in pilot tenants.

Console UX and Customer-facing messaging
- Console should show: current SLO SKU per route, estimated monthly spend (based on rolling 30-day traffic), and a simulator to model changes (latency and fidelity).
- Messaging: emphasize predictability, ability to pin fidelity for critical routes, and credits for migration. Avoid technical jargon in first-touch sales material.

Developer API contract (examples)
- Customers may request a preferred SLO via request headers for best-effort routing. Example header: 
  X-Redwood-SLO: latency=p95<=200ms; fidelity=enhanced
- If header cannot be honored, server responds with HTTP 202 + retry-after header when queued, or 200 with response indicating lowered fidelity and billing note in response metadata.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Incorrect latency attribution leading to customer disputes. Mitigation: dual-write raw events to durable audit store and provide replay tooling for disputes.
- Risk: Revenue erosion from grace-window billing of fallbacks. Mitigation: limit grace-window to 30s and require policy approval for exceptions.

Open questions (product/finance backlog)
- Final SKU price points and volume discounts by tenant committed throughput.
- Whether to bill by measured p95 or by configurable latency SLO that customers can set per-contract.

Appendix: mapping from existing token billing to meter units (example heuristic)
- For text-generation requests: 1 meter unit ~ 1 request; optional multiplier for very long responses (>200 tokens) where token surcharge applies: surcharge = ceil(tokens/200) * 0.25 meter units.

FAQ
Q: Will customers be forced to change models?
A: No. This model bills based on requested SLOs; customers can opt to keep token-only plans during the migration window.

Q: How do we handle multi-tenant Dedicated pools?
A: Dedicated contracts can be metered at the tenant-level and reconciled monthly; for shared tenant pools, we offer a fractional-capacity SKU (see related pricing playbooks).
